owner: CC owns the measure and the migration mechanism. Akien owns 'under way' — what counts as history that still establishes right-now vs history that has silently become an archive.
state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME -> PROVED
intention: Law 5's new bound: nothing derives whether a component's history still establishes right-now, nothing moves the rest to the commons, and nothing reds a working surface that has silently become an archive. MEASURED on the day the Law was restated: 33 history.json files in class-space, and slates/ at 96 stored against exactly 1 the reader ever loads — the rule violated 95:1 inside the very artifact whose job is telling the next mind what is going on. This ticket adds a measure of REACH (how deep is history actually read?) that feeds a migration the door performs — history past 'under way' moves to the commons, and something notices when it should have moved but hasn't.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM: a mind stands in a component directory to be briefed (Law 5's promise), opens history.json, and finds 30 entries spanning months. Most of them are about voyages long since proved. The history is formally correct — everything there really happened — but it no longer establishes what is going on RIGHT NOW, and the mind has to read all of it to discover that. That is re-deriving a settled answer (Law 1), and the cost scales with the length of the history, not the complexity of the current work. Slates are worse: 96 files sit in the store, the reader loads 1, and the other 95 are invisible weight.
traces_to: Law 5 — intent, its current state, and its proofs share an address, and the address carries what a mind needs NOW. History of a thing under way belongs beside it; history past that is noise at the working surface and berths in the commons instead.

Law 1 — the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled. A 30-entry history.json where 28 entries are about proved work is 28 re-derivations of 'this is not what is going on right now'.
Law 4 — 'under way' is a word a reader has to apply by hand; the migration should be physics.
gates: A measure of reach — how much of each history file is actually read by arriving minds — feeding a migration mechanism. The migration moves history entries that are no longer 'under way' to the commons, where they are kept and greppable (never destroyed). Something notices when history should have moved but hasn't. The mechanism is design work for BUILDME.
falsifier: RED if: (1) history that stopped being under way stays at the working surface with nothing noticing; (2) the migration destroys history instead of moving it to the commons — 'we're not saying DESTROY ALL HISTORY'; (3) the reach measure counts file existence instead of actual reads — a file nobody opens scores the same as a file read every session; (4) slates/ is excluded — it is the same shape at 96:1 and the same Law.
horizon: Not urgent in isolation, but this is the same gap that state-and-history-door-catches-in-place-edits names from the enforcement side. The two could share a build.
dependencies: MEASURED: 33 history.json in class-space, slates at 96:1. The measurement is the baseline.
'Under way' needs a definition the door can apply. A PROVED ticket's history is clearly past under-way. A BUILDME ticket's history is clearly still under way. The boundary is the design question.
distinctions_recorded: MOVING IS NOT DELETING. The commons keeps the history and it stays greppable. The working surface loses it because the working surface is for what is going on NOW.
REACH IS NOT EXISTENCE. A history file that exists but nobody reads is worse than no file — it impersonates a briefing surface while being an archive. The measure must be about actual utility.
provenance: Born as an IOU in CLAUDE.md's 'Rules awaiting physics' section under Law 5's new bound. Measured 2026-08-17 when the Law was restated. Ticketed 2026-08-21 to retire the 'ticket owed' marker.
